units.passage: AI may be used to help you come up with interesting ways to present your findings.
units.why: 'AI may be used to help you come up with interesting ways to present your findings' (P15).

units.passage: Use tools to brainstorm, find examples that may be useful to review, pose questions that will help you go further into the topic at hand.
units.why: Permitted: 'Use tools to brainstorm, find examples ... pose questions': P15.

units.passage: Students are permitted to use AI (including text bots like ChatGPT and Claude, as well as writing assistants like Grammarly) to brainstorm for and edit assignments.
units.why: 'Students are permitted to use AI ... to brainstorm for and edit assignments' (P15).
units.fit_note: Also covers editing.

units.passage: Planning: Goblin.tools has a “Magic ToDo”, which can help you break down more complicated tasks into smaller action items.
units.why: Names a specific tool for breaking tasks into steps for planning; AI for planning and exploring approaches fits P15 best.
units.fit_note: Task planning rather than idea generation; also names a recommended tool. | AI for breaking a task into steps, not brainstorming ideas.

units.passage: You may use Generative AI to help you in the initial stages of your assignments, but you must ensure that your work goes beyond the Generative AI output.
units.why: Allows AI in 'the initial stages' of assignments but requires work to 'go beyond the Generative AI output'; brainstorming and outlining allowed (P15) with a keep-thinking condition.

units.passage: In this course, you may use AI tools such as ChatGPT and DALL●E 2 to brainstorm ideas and create outlines.
units.why: Option B says students 'may use AI tools such as ChatGPT and DALL-E 2 to brainstorm ideas and create outlines'; this permits AI for brainstorming (P15) while students work on assignments.

units.passage: This faculty guide highlights how generative AI can help address common student learning challenges by supporting brainstorming, organizing ideas, understanding difficult concepts, and revising written work. It provides practical examples of how students can use AI to enhance learning while still engaging in critical thinking, communication, and the development of academic skills.
units.why: The guide 'highlights how generative AI can help ... by supporting brainstorming, organizing ideas, understanding difficult concepts, and revising written work'. It is a description addressed to instructors of what student uses are valuable, so actor is instructor, modality informs, stance encourage.
units.fit_note: Lists several permitted uses (brainstorming, organizing, concept understanding, revising writing) that span P12, P15 and P18. | Also covers explaining concepts (P12) and revising prose (P18).

units.passage: You may use AI programs (e.g., ChatGPT) to help generate ideas and brainstorm.
units.why: Example 1: "You may use AI programs ... to help generate ideas and brainstorm" is a brainstorming permission, so P15.

units.passage: Utilizing them effectively involves employing them for idea generation, synthesis, and information gathering to gain a comprehensive understanding of various topics.
units.policy: Using AI tools effectively involves employing them for idea generation, synthesis, and information gathering to gain a comprehensive understanding of various topics.
units.why: Example 2 compares AI to calculators, "incredible assistants", and welcomes use for "idea generation, synthesis, and information gathering"; P15 fits partly because the uses also include synthesis and gathering, noted in fit_note.
units.fit_note: Also covers synthesis and information gathering, not only brainstorming. Coder B: Also names synthesis and information gathering.

units.passage: If generative AI is permitted by the instructor (for brainstorming, outlining, etc.), students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge the use, since it is an algorithm rather than a source.
units.why: 'If generative AI is permitted by the instructor (for brainstorming, outlining, etc.)' gives brainstorming and outlining as example permitted uses, gated by the instructor. P15 (brainstorming) is the nearest type; fit_note notes the instructor gate.
units.fit_note: Brainstorming and outlining are only examples, and are allowed only if the instructor permits AI. / Also covers outlining and makes permission depend on the instructor.

units.passage: Se permite el uso de las herramientas de la IA únicamente para consultas generales, como generación de ideas, investigación inicial o revisión de conceptos básicos.
units.why: Level 1 permits AI "únicamente para consultas generales, como generación de ideas, investigación inicial o revisión de conceptos básicos"; brainstorming leads the list so P15.
units.fit_note: Also covers initial research and reviewing basic concepts, limited to general consultation. | Also covers initial research and review of basic concepts, and limits AI to these general queries only.

units.passage: Puede(s) utilizar herramienta(s) de Inteligencia Artificial únicamente para actividades previas a una tarea o un trabajo académico, como la lluvia de ideas, la planificación o la investigación inicial.
units.why: Level 1 sample text allows AI only "para actividades previas a una tarea", such as brainstorming and planning; nearest P15 but the limit to pre-task use is extra.
units.fit_note: AI is limited to pre-task activities (brainstorming, planning, initial research), not only brainstorming.

units.passage: Some generative AI: Although generative AI can be used as a tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas), work submitted by a student should be that of the student and not the work of an AI system.
units.why: Option 3 allows AI 'to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)'. Ideas fits brainstorming (P15); feedback is not captured, so noted.
units.fit_note: Also permits obtaining feedback, which P15 does not name. | Also permits AI for obtaining feedback, which no single type covers.

units.passage: Using AI sources can be helpful for students to brainstorm, edit, translate, or generate ideas for their academic work.
units.why: States AI use 'can be helpful for students to brainstorm, edit, translate, or generate ideas'; names permitted uses. P15 chosen as first-listed; editing and translation are prose uses (P18).
units.fit_note: Also lists editing and translating, which are prose uses (P18).

units.passage: Use of AI such as ChatGPT is only permitted to help you brainstorm ideas and see examples. All material you submit must be your own.
units.why: Sample statement allowing AI only to brainstorm and see examples, with submitted material the student's own; a narrow permission, P15 (brainstorming).
units.fit_note: Also says all submitted material must be the student's own (P29).

units.passage: use to organize ideas in a first draft;
units.why: 'use to organize ideas in a first draft' lists a writing-support use of AI; P15 (brainstorming and exploring approaches) is the nearest type because P18 is about prose versus code.
units.fit_note: P18 is about prose versus code; this unit is about organizing ideas in a first draft (P15). Coder B's own reading: lists a writing-support use.

units.passage: Use of AI such as ChatGPT is only permitted to help you brainstorm ideas and see examples. All material you submit must be your own.
units.why: The sample 'only permitted to help you brainstorm ideas and see examples. All material you submit must be your own' limits AI to brainstorming; P15 fits, with the added rule that submitted material be the student's own.
units.fit_note: Sample statement; also requires that all submitted material be the student's own. | Sample statement; the only allowed use is brainstorming and seeing examples.

units.passage: AI can be used in a variety of ways in college courses: practice language skills when learning another language; use to organize ideas in a first draft
units.why: The FAQ lists 'use to organize ideas in a first draft' among ways AI can be used in college courses. It is a general list of uses (actor all), a permission (may, permit); it is closest to brainstorming and exploring approaches (P15). P18 (prose versus code) does not fit.
units.fit_note: Organizing ideas in a first draft is a writing use; P15 (brainstorming and exploring) is the nearest type, and no type covers general writing assistance. | Listed as a general possibility, not a rule with conditions.

units.passage: AI can be used in a variety of ways in college courses: practice language skills when learning another language; use to organize ideas in a first draft; finding and organizing information in research papers; generate opposing arguments for discussions; create questions for content knowledge self-assessments; use as personalized tutor for improving learning.
units.why: Lists a use: 'generate opposing arguments for discussions'; exploring alternative viewpoints, P15.

units.passage: Asking Generative AIs to provide high-level, non-library, or code-level guidance, e.g., "I found the sklearn clustering page helpful," and " I found the shapenet dataset useful."
units.why: MECH 294: 'Asking Generative AIs to provide high-level, non-library, or code-level guidance' is OK; exploring approaches, P15.
units.fit_note: Examples are pointers to libraries and datasets. Guidance on resources such as libraries and datasets.

units.passage: Example a. GenAI tools are permitted for brainstorming and outlining only (with disclosure)
units.why: Example a is wording a faculty member may insert in a syllabus: "GenAI tools are permitted for brainstorming and outlining only (with disclosure)". It is addressed to instructors who write the syllabus (before-course), may, and limits use to listed tasks with disclosure; brainstorming and outlining fit P15.
units.fit_note: Also outlining, only, and requires disclosure.

units.passage: Brainstorming and Idea Generation: Using GenAI to explore topics, generate initial ideas, or refine research questions.
units.why: "Brainstorming and Idea Generation: Using GenAI to explore topics, generate initial ideas, or refine research questions" is permitted by default (P15).

units.passage: GenAI can help individuals brainstorm, iterate, and explore multiple angles when individuals actively question, verify and refine outputs rather than accept them outright.
units.why: "GenAI can help individuals brainstorm, iterate, and explore multiple angles" permits brainstorming and exploring approaches, conditioned on questioning and verifying output; P15.

units.passage: Expand on ideas for projects or papers
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to expand on ideas for projects or papers.
units.why: "Expand on ideas for projects or papers" is a listed learning use, brainstorming, P15.

units.passage: Explore examples, such as sample code or problem‑solving steps
units.policy: When appropriate for context and discipline, GenAI might be used to explore examples, such as sample code or problem-solving steps.
units.why: "Explore examples, such as sample code or problem-solving steps" is a listed use that explores approaches, so P15.
units.fit_note: Sample code is named; submission of AI code is not addressed. | Names sample code explicitly.

units.passage: This includes using it to brainstorm, summarize complex texts, or compare AI-generated and human-written responses,
units.why: Example uses "to brainstorm, summarize complex texts, or compare AI-generated and human-written responses"; brainstorming is the lead use so P15.
units.fit_note: Also lists summarizing texts and comparing AI and human responses.

units.passage: The use of AI as a reference tool, for ideation, research assistance, translation and tutoring purposes is permitted, at faculty discretion, provided it is clearly 5 | Page acknowledged and cited in any work submitted
units.policy: The use of AI for ideation is permitted, at faculty discretion, provided it is clearly acknowledged and cited in any work submitted.
units.why: The same sentence permits AI "for ideation", i.e. brainstorming, so P15.

units.passage: These tools can assist in brainstorming, researching, and exploring complex concepts.
units.why: Tier 3 names uses: 'brainstorming, researching, and exploring complex concepts'; brainstorming is the main permission.
units.fit_note: Also lists researching and exploring concepts (P12 tutor use), grouped here under P15 for brainstorming.

units.passage: Brainstorming creative project ideas and themes
units.why: "Brainstorming creative project ideas and themes" is a listed potential use, matching P15.

units.passage: Brainstorming and refining your ideas;
units.why: "Brainstorming and refining your ideas" is listed under the activities for which generative AI "is permitted in this course", so it allows AI for brainstorming (P15).

units.passage: Fine tuning your research questions;
units.why: "Fine tuning your research questions" is a permitted exploratory use; P15 (exploring approaches) is the nearest type.

units.passage: They can help you get started and brainstorm–help to “stimulate thought and develop drafts that are still [your] own work
units.why: The page names brainstorming and getting started as a benefit, quoting the MLA-CCCC task force: AI for brainstorming, P15.

units.passage: You can choose to use AI tools to help brainstorm assignments or projects
units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst, encouraged): students "can choose to use AI tools to help brainstorm"; brainstorming, P15.
units.fit_note: Also allows AI to revise one's own written work (P91).

units.passage: Students are invited to use AI platforms to help prepare for assignments and projects
units.why: Sample (Iowa, encouraged): students "are invited to use AI platforms to help prepare for assignments" e.g. brainstorming; P15.

units.passage: Use Ai for inspiration, not as a final submission
units.why: "Brainstorm and generate ideas: Use Ai for inspiration, not as a final submission"; brainstorming, P15.
units.fit_note: Adds that AI output is not the final submission. | Also bars submitting AI output as the final work (P19).

units.passage: You may use AI tools to brainstorm ideas or plan your approach.
units.why: Sample 'AI for Brainstorming or Early Stages': 'You may use AI tools to brainstorm ideas or plan your approach', a narrow permitted use, P15.

units.passage: You may use generative AI for learning support and planning, such as explaining concepts, generating practice questions, brainstorming ideas, or creating a preliminary outline.
units.why: Level 1 allows 'brainstorming ideas, or creating a preliminary outline', P15.

units.passage: you are welcome to use ChatGPT or another AI tool to assist you with brainstorming ideas, creating an outline, and drafting your first version of the text.
units.why: The sample says students 'are welcome to use ChatGPT or another AI tool to assist you with brainstorming ideas, creating an outline, and drafting your first version', a permitted use, P15 (brainstorming), with drafting as extra.
units.fit_note: Also allows outlining and drafting a first version. / Also permits drafting a first version, not only brainstorming.

units.passage: You are invited to use AI tools strategically in this course—to brainstorm, draft, analyze, or revise.
units.why: "to brainstorm, draft, analyze, or revise" lists permitted uses; brainstorming is the specific permission, P15, though drafting and revising go wider.
units.fit_note: Also permits drafting, analyzing and revising, not only brainstorming. Also lists drafting, analyzing and revising, which span P91 and P89.

units.passage: e.g., to generate research questions or draft outlines
units.why: "to generate research questions or draft outlines" gives example permitted uses in the mixed-use policy, brainstorming and outlining; P15.
units.fit_note: Examples only; permission applies only where assignment instructions allow.

units.passage: Brainstorming initial topic ideas or approaches (after you have spent some time thinking on your own)
units.why: Permitted: "Brainstorming initial topic ideas or approaches" after thinking alone; P15.
units.fit_note: Condition: think on your own first. Allowed only after own thinking first.

units.passage: AI use is allowed with the brainstorming and preparation of assignments and project milestones.
units.why: PSY 32 policy: "AI use is allowed with the brainstorming and preparation of assignments", AI for brainstorming, P15.
units.fit_note: Also covers preparation of assignments and milestones.

units.passage: Using AI to generate examples, counterarguments, or alternative perspectives that help you develop more nuanced thinking
units.why: Recommended: generating "examples, counterarguments, or alternative perspectives", exploring approaches, P15.

units.passage: Generating multiple approaches or possibilities (after thinking on your own first) to expand your options
units.why: Recommended: "Generating multiple approaches or possibilities" after thinking alone, P15.
units.fit_note: Allowed after the student's own thinking first.

units.passage: AI can help students with outlining, idea generation, and deeper engagement with concepts
units.why: "AI can help students with outlining, idea generation, and deeper engagement with concepts" names idea generation as a use; brainstorming is P15 (the outlining and writing-tutor parts are coded separately).

units.passage: Brainstorming and Idea Generation: Using AI to help explore potential directions or organize thoughts
units.policy: Acceptable use of AI: brainstorming and idea generation, using AI to help explore potential directions or organize thoughts.
units.why: The examples list 'Brainstorming and Idea Generation' as acceptable, so AI may be used to explore directions; P15.

units.passage: You use AI to help brainstorm, build outlines, search for tools, explain concepts, and generate ideas, but the actual content you submit is your own
units.why: Level 2 lets students 'use AI to help brainstorm, build outlines, search for tools, explain concepts, and generate ideas', a permission for brainstorming and structuring: P15.
units.fit_note: Also covers explaining concepts and searching for tools, beyond brainstorming.

units.passage: They should define acceptable use cases (e.g. brainstorming ideas, improving grammar, changing linguistic style) versus prohibited uses (e.g. submitting AI-generated text as one’s own work)
units.why: 'acceptable use cases (e.g. brainstorming ideas, improving grammar, changing linguistic style)' gives examples of allowed uses: P15, noting that grammar and style help also appears.
units.fit_note: Also names grammar and style editing as examples of acceptable use. Also covers grammar and style help (P91).

units.passage: Teaching students how to brainstorm with generative AI can help students how to effectively use it and where it can be most effective
units.why: 'Teaching students how to brainstorm with generative AI can help students how to effectively use it' supports AI for brainstorming: P15.

units.passage: Brainstorming ideas
units.why: 'Brainstorming ideas' is a listed permitted purpose in the template: P15.

units.passage: AI-assisted writing is acceptable.
units.why: The model statement "AI-assisted writing is acceptable ... not to generate text" allows AI for ideas and feedback while barring generated text; I coded it P15 because the permitted use named first is idea generation.
units.fit_note: Sample statement; also limits generation to 3 iterations of 150 words and separates assistance from generation (P18).

units.passage: You can choose to use AI tools to help brainstorm assignments or projects or to revise existing work you have written.
units.why: 'You can choose to use AI tools to help brainstorm assignments or projects or to revise existing work you have written' permits brainstorming and revision. P15 fits for brainstorming; revision is part of the same permission.
units.fit_note: Coder A (P15): Also permits revising one's own work (P91). Coder B (P15): Also allows revising own work and requires attribution of AI text (colored font, quotation or citation).

units.passage: Generative AI can be useful in helping students generate things to consider about their projects, such as headings or titles, or even questions they should consider.
units.why: 'Generative AI can be useful in helping students generate things to consider about their projects, such as headings or titles' names brainstorming. P15 fits.

units.passage: You might ask about ideas or topics and use the output to further narrow or broaden areas you are interested in researching further.
units.why: 'You might ask about ideas or topics and use the output to further narrow or broaden areas you are interested in researching' lists brainstorming as a use. P15 fits.

units.passage: Give it your draft or a section of your text and ask for title and heading suggestions.
units.why: 'Give it your draft or a section of your text and ask for title and heading suggestions' lists headings as a use. P15 fits.

units.passage: Any assignment requiring use of AI will be clearly outlined in the assignment instructions and may include tasks such as brainstorming, analyzing information or editing.
units.why: Permitted tasks 'may include tasks such as brainstorming, analyzing information or editing'; brainstorming (P15) is the first listed, but analysis (P89) and editing (P91) are also named.
units.fit_note: Also lists analyzing information (P89) and editing (P91) in one list.

units.passage: Ideation and Research (AI can be used to help generate ideas, organization and information gathering
units.why: 'Ideation and Research (AI can be used to help generate ideas, organization and information gathering)' permits brainstorming (P15); student, during-work, may.

units.passage: You may use AI tools on your assignments for brainstorming only. This means that you can use AI to generate some initial ideas or inspiration
units.why: 'You may use AI tools on your assignments for brainstorming only' allows AI for idea generation, P15.

units.passage: To access just-in-time support at various stages of the learning process: generating or testing out ideas or formulas; summarizing or distilling complex thinking; learning specific genre conventions; checking grammar
units.why: 'generating or testing out ideas or formulas' as a potential student use is brainstorming and exploration (P15).
units.fit_note: Same sentence also lists summarizing, genre conventions and grammar checking.

units.passage: In this course, it is permitted to use Generative AI chat services such as ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, and Claude as a tool to aid in your understanding of content, to develop ideas, and edit drafts of your work.
units.why: The same sentence permits using AI "to develop ideas", i.e. brainstorming, P15.
